q: Name a product or service that Google shut down.
hint: Includes Alphabet units like YouTube, Nest and Waze. Plain renames don't count.

answers.l: Google's RSS reader, shut down on July 1, 2013. Its closure became the standard example in any argument about trusting a Google product.
Consumer Google+ closed in April 2019, months after Google disclosed an API bug that had exposed users' profile data.
Cloud gaming service launched in November 2019 and shut down in January 2023; Google refunded hardware and game purchases.
Real-time collaboration platform unveiled at Google I/O 2009; Google stopped development in 2010 and handed the code to Apache.
Head-mounted display whose Explorer Edition shipped in 2013; Google ended sales of the Enterprise Edition in March 2023.
Experimental Gmail client launched in 2014 with bundles and snoozing; shut down in 2019.
Unified messaging app launched in 2013; Google moved users to Google Chat and shut Hangouts down in 2022.
Social network named after its creator, engineer Orkut Büyükkökten; hugely popular in Brazil and India, closed in September 2014.
Photo organizer Google acquired in 2004; retired in 2016 in favor of Google Photos.
Messaging app launched in 2016 with Google Assistant built in; shut down in March 2019.
Music store and streaming service that launched as Google Music in 2011; replaced by YouTube Music and shut down in 2020.
Social feed built into Gmail in February 2010; its auto-follow privacy backlash led to an FTC settlement, and it closed in 2011.
Customizable start page of gadgets launched in 2005; shut down on November 1, 2013.
Domain registrar launched in 2014; Google sold its registrations to Squarespace in 2023.
Podcast app shut down in 2024, with Google pointing listeners to YouTube Music.
Streaming dongle launched in 2013 for $35; Google discontinued the line in 2024 in favor of the Google TV Streamer.
Open source project hosting launched in 2006; went read-only in 2015 and closed in January 2016 as projects moved to GitHub.
XMPP-based chat launched in 2005; replaced by Hangouts and fully retired in 2017.
Google-branded Android devices from the Nexus One in 2010 to the Nexus 6P; replaced by the Pixel line in 2016.
Video hosting service that lost to YouTube; Google bought YouTube in 2006 and moved remaining Google Video uploads there in 2012.
Paid Q&A service where vetted researchers answered questions for a fee; stopped taking new questions in late 2006.
Desktop search tool that indexed local files and email; discontinued in 2011 as operating systems built in their own search.
Browser plugin for offline web apps launched in 2007; dropped as HTML5 standardized the same features.
Let any device print to any printer through Google's cloud; shut down on December 31, 2020.
Personal health record service launched in 2008; shut down in 2012 after failing to gain wide use.
Real-time friend location sharing in Google Maps; retired in August 2013.
Clip-and-save research tool; development stopped in 2009 and remaining notes moved to Google Docs in 2012.
The goo.gl service stopped creating new short links in 2019, with Google recommending Firebase Dynamic Links instead.
Google ended long-term support for AngularJS on December 31, 2021, leaving the rewritten Angular as its successor.
Android VR platform launched in 2016; discontinued in 2019 when the Pixel 4 shipped without support for it.
Folded-cardboard VR viewer handed out at Google I/O 2014; Google open-sourced the project in 2019 and stopped selling viewers in 2021.
Modular smartphone with swappable hardware components; Google cancelled it in 2016.
Author-credited encyclopedia widely seen as a Wikipedia rival; launched in 2008 and closed in 2012.
Estimated flu activity from search queries; stopped publishing in 2015 after it badly overestimated flu levels in 2013.
Programming competition run since 2003; Google ended it in 2023 along with Hash Code and Kick Start.
Data table and mapping tool from Google Research; shut down in December 2019.
A/B testing tool for websites tied to Google Analytics; shut down on September 30, 2023.
Previous version of Google Analytics; standard properties stopped processing data on July 1, 2023, forcing a move to GA4.
55-inch digital whiteboard with a companion app; Google ended the Jamboard app at the end of 2024.
Small camera that used on-device AI to decide which moments to capture; discontinued in 2019.
Spherical media streamer shown at Google I/O 2012; given to attendees but never released for sale.
Online payment service launched in 2006; merged into Google Wallet in 2013.
Group sharing app launched in May 2016 and shut down less than a year later.
Audio-only Chromecast for plugging into speakers, launched in 2015; discontinued in January 2019.
Clickable text overlays on videos; YouTube deleted all existing annotations in January 2019.
Premium Chromebook launched in 2017; Google cancelled its successor and ended the line in 2022.
Browser toolbar launched in 2000 that showed each page's PageRank; discontinued as Chrome replaced it.
3D avatar chat rooms launched in July 2008 and closed by the end of that same year.
Yellow rack-mounted server that indexed corporate intranets; Google announced its phase-out in 2016.
Travel itinerary app launched in 2016; removed in 2019 with its features folded into Search and Maps.
Android push messaging service; replaced by Firebase Cloud Messaging and shut down in 2019.
Ran sandboxed native code inside Chrome; deprecated in 2017 in favor of WebAssembly.
Plugin that put Chrome's rendering engine inside Internet Explorer; retired in early 2014.
Geotagged photo-sharing site whose pictures appeared as a layer in Google Earth; shut down in November 2016.
Let users edit Google Maps directly; closed in 2017 after vandalism such as a 2015 edit showing an Android robot urinating on an Apple logo.
Android variant for IoT devices announced in 2016; Google shut down its developer console in 2022.
Depth-sensing augmented reality platform for phones; ended in 2018 as Google shifted to ARCore.
Live broadcasting version of Hangouts; shut down in 2019 with users moved to YouTube Live.
Web bookmark-saving service; shut down in September 2021.
Workspace replacement for enterprise Google+; shut down in 2023 in favor of Spaces in Google Chat.
VR field trip app for classrooms; shut down in June 2021, with many tours moved to Google Arts & Culture.
Google's library of 3D models for VR and AR creators; shut down in June 2021.
Applicant tracking system for G Suite customers; shut down in September 2020.
Google's online coding rounds, often used as a hiring funnel; ended in 2023.
Team programming competition that began in France in 2014; Google ended it in 2023.
Google Cloud's Docker image registry at gcr.io; deprecated in favor of Artifact Registry.
Deep links that survived app installs; deprecated in 2023 and shut down in August 2025.
Home alarm system from Nest; Google ended support for it in April 2024.
Wi-Fi camera startup Nest acquired in 2014; Google ended support for the original Dropcam cameras in 2024.
Developer program for third-party Nest integrations; Google announced its shutdown in 2019 in favor of Works with Google Assistant.
Smart home hub Nest acquired in 2014; its servers were shut off in May 2016, turning customers' hubs into bricks.
Google's public showcase for experimental products; shut down in 2011 as Larry Page narrowed the company's focus.
Regex search over public source code; shut down in January 2012. Russ Cox later explained how it worked using trigram indexes.
SMS check-in service Google bought in 2005 and closed in 2009; co-founder Dennis Crowley later co-founded Foursquare.
Lightweight YouTube app for low-bandwidth markets with offline saving; discontinued in 2022.
Standalone gaming app launched in 2015 to compete with Twitch; shut down in 2019.
Subscription bundling a Pixel phone with Google One and YouTube Premium; discontinued in August 2023.
Online photo albums tied to Picasa; replaced by Google Photos in 2016.
Google's first own-brand Chromebook, launched in 2013 with a high-resolution touchscreen; later replaced by the Pixelbook.
Daily deals service launched in 2011 to compete with Groupon; shut down in 2014.
Low-code app builder for G Suite; shut down in January 2021.
Contest that introduced pre-university students to open source; last held in 2019.
Public Wi-Fi program launched in Indian railway stations with RailTel; ended in 2020.
Editor for human translators built on Google Translate; shut down in December 2019.
Found search terms whose popularity matched a time series you supplied; shut down in December 2019.
Managed device connection service on Google Cloud; retired in August 2023.
Took snapshots of running production code without stopping it; Google retired it in 2023.
Wi-Fi router built with TP-Link and Asus, launched in 2015; Google ended support for it in 2022.
Physical debit card that spent your Google Wallet balance; discontinued in 2016.
Site for sharing and discovering things you planned to do; shut down in 2014.
Let crowds submit and vote on questions for events and Q&As; shut down in 2015.
Let users model 3D buildings for Google Earth from aerial photos; retired in 2013.
Game based on Luis von Ahn's ESP Game where paired players tagged images; shut down in 2011.
Labs experiment that returned search results as a table of facts; closed in 2011.
Browser sidebar for leaving comments on any web page; shut down in 2011.
Showed household electricity use from smart meters; retired in 2011.
Added social features like member lists to third-party sites; retired for non-Blogger sites in 2012.
Search volume analysis tool that was merged into Google Trends in 2012.
Free database for listings like products and jobs; replaced by Google Merchant Center in 2010.
Simple website builder; closed in 2008 with users moved to Google Sites.
Firefox extension that synced bookmarks, cookies and passwords; discontinued in 2008.
Prefetching proxy released in 2005 that followed links in web apps, sometimes triggering deletes; discontinued in 2008.
Finnish microblogging service Google bought in 2007; shut down in 2012.
Social Q&A service that routed questions to people in your network; Google bought it in 2010 and shut it down in 2011.
Web-based chat startup Google acquired in 2012; its products were shut down after the deal.
Online photo editor Google acquired in 2010; shut down in April 2012.
Shared contacts and photos when two phones were bumped together; Google bought it in 2013 and shut it down in early 2014.
Music curation service Google acquired in 2014; shut down in 2016 and folded into Google Play Music.
Email security company Google acquired for $625 million in 2007; its services were folded into Google Apps and retired.
Waze feature that matched commuters for shared rides; shut down in 2022.
Built-in browser editor for trimming and combining YouTube uploads; removed in September 2017.
Short-lived creator updates first tested as YouTube Reels; ended in June 2023.
Converted Flash animations and ads to HTML5; shut down in 2016.
Held old photos from Picasa Web Albums and Google+; shut down in 2023.
Assistant feature that filled out web forms, such as car rental bookings, on the user's behalf; shut down in 2022.
Android home screen app that put Google Now one swipe from the home screen; Google stopped distributing it in 2017.
Ran the Android Auto interface on the phone itself; discontinued in 2022 in favor of Google Assistant driving mode.
Web directory built on DMOZ, the Open Directory Project; shut down in 2011.
Tool for building mashups of Google APIs; shut down in 2009 with users steered to App Engine.
Area 120 app for finding local activities with people who share your interests; shut down in 2020.
Area 120 local Q&A app launched in India in 2018; shut down in 2020.
Area 120 project combining spreadsheets and databases; shut down with users pointed to AppSheet.
Tablet app for browsing digital versions of retail catalogs.
Property listings shown on Google Maps; shut down in 2011.
Free bundle of Google and third-party desktop software; discontinued in 2011.
Let readers flip through screenshots of news articles; closed in 2011 along with Google Labs.
Sold radio ad placements after Google bought dMarc Broadcasting; ended in 2009.
Sold newspaper ad space through AdWords; ended in 2009.
Social app maker founded by Max Levchin; Google acquired it in 2010 and shut it down in 2011.
Let viewers submit subtitles and translations for videos; removed in September 2020.
Private messaging inside the YouTube app; removed in September 2019.
Plugin that synced Microsoft Office files with Google Docs; retired in 2013.
Android's first push service, known as C2DM; deprecated in 2012 in favor of Google Cloud Messaging.
Let people pay a monthly fee to see fewer ads on participating websites.
Enterprise tool for hosting and publishing custom map data; shut down in 2016.
Smaller sibling of the Google Search Appliance for small businesses; discontinued in 2012.

nope.Gmail: Still running. Inbox by Gmail was the Gmail client that got shut down.
nope.Google Duo: Merged into Google Meet in 2022, which counts as a rename.
nope.Bard: Renamed Gemini in 2024; the product lives on.
nope.Android Pay: Rebranded as Google Pay in 2018 rather than shut down.
nope.Google Wallet: Still active; Google revived the name for its payment app in 2022.
nope.SketchUp: Sold to Trimble in 2012 and still sold today.
nope.Google Fiber: Expansion paused in 2016, but the service still operates.
nope.Google Nose: A 2013 April Fools' joke, never a real product.
nope.Vine: Shut down by Twitter, not Google.

traps.q: Which Google product's 2013 shutdown became the standard example of Google killing a beloved service?
traps.l: Announced in a March 2013 spring cleaning and shut down July 1, 2013; Feedly and other RSS readers saw a rush of new users.

traps.q: Which Google social network, named after the engineer who built it, was a hit in Brazil and India?
traps.l: Built by Orkut Büyükkökten and launched in January 2004; Google closed it in September 2014.
